summary: Iteration 5 validated the two-page PDF bug fix AND the visual contrast polish for all 3 invoice templates. (1) PDF Page-count: For TE/2026-27/0001, downloaded PDFs for Modern Corporate, Government Supply, and Compact Single-Page — all three produced exactly 1 page (verified via pypdf.PdfReader). File sizes reasonable (255-400 KB, JPEG-embedded a4-page snapshots). (2) Visual contrast — during grayscale simulation and normal color inspection, I discovered a REAL residual contrast bug the initial CSS polish had missed: `.a4-page td { color: #0a0a0a }` (line 91) and `.a4-page .font-mono { color: #0a0a0a }` (line 95) set a directly-applied dark color on child cells / mono spans, which overrides the parent's `text-white` (inheritance loses to a child's own declared value, even when the parent's rule is !important). Impact: (a) Modern's invoice number 'TE/2026-27/0001' inside the top-right blue box was BLACK ON BLACK (invisible), (b) Modern's Grand Total amount '₹ 52,156.00' (font-mono span inside bg-slate-900 bar) was invisible, (c) Gem's GRAND TOTAL row (both TDs inside bg-slate-900 tr) had 'GRAND TOTAL' and '₹ 52,156.00' invisible. FIXED here in /app/frontend/src/index.css by adding scoped `.a4-page .bg-slate-900 td/th/.num/.font-mono/span/div { color:#fff !important }` (plus same for bg-blue-600, bg-[#0F172A], bg-amber-600/700). Re-ran all 3 templates: color + grayscale screenshots now show every dark-background label and number crisply white and fully legible. PDFs still 1 page after fix.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by test agent — `.a4-page td { color:#0a0a0a }` and `.a4-page .font-mono { color:#0a0a0a }` rendered white-on-dark text INVISIBLE (Modern invoice-number chip, Modern Grand Total amount, Gem GRAND TOTAL row). Added scoped rules for bg-slate-900 / bg-blue-600 / bg-[#0F172A] / bg-amber-600/700 to force child cells + mono spans + generic descendants to white with !important. Original CSS polish had `.a4-page .text-white{color:#fff!important}` but that only helps elements that literally carry the class `text-white`; the actual failing children (td, font-mono) don't carry that class and their own `.a4-page td{color:#0a0a0a}` rule beat the parent's inherited color.

OPTIONAL follow-up (not tested here — deferred to avoid touching user's live ledger data): the multi-page legitimate-overflow test (create a 20-line-item invoice, verify PDF > 1 page with no blank pages between). The slicing loop `while (renderedPx < canvas.height - 1)` + trailing skip `sliceHpx < pxPerMm * 20` mathematically guarantees correct multi-page behavior for tall content, and single-page was proven; but if you want empirical proof, run it in staging with a disposable invoice + counter rollback.
critical_code_review_comments: CSS specificity trap in .a4-page: rules like `.a4-page td { color: #0a0a0a }` set color DIRECTLY on td/th cells, which defeats `color: inherit` from a parent tr's text-white. `!important` on the parent's `.text-white` rule does not cascade — child elements with their own explicit color declaration always win over inherited color regardless of the parent's !important. Fix must scope by dark-bg ancestor (as added).

The .a4-page CSS block (index.css lines 78-155) is doing a lot — it acts as a print-media reset AND overrides many tailwind utilities. Consider extracting into /app/frontend/src/styles/a4-print.css and adding a comment header documenting each override's intent.

download() in InvoicePreview.jsx sets el.style.minHeight='auto' then restores in finally — good. But if html2canvas throws mid-render, the modal already shows the collapsed layout until finally runs — acceptable in practice but consider using CSS class toggle instead of inline style for cleaner style-restoration semantics.

trailing-slice guard `sliceHpx < pxPerMm * 20` (20mm ≈ 76px @ scale 2) is a reasonable threshold. If a legitimate final page had only 15mm of content it would be dropped — worth documenting the trade-off.

rca of the issue: Two-page bug (fixed by main agent): `.a4-page { min-height: 297mm }` forced the DOM node to always be full A4 tall, so html2canvas captured trailing whitespace which the slicer then split into a second (blank) page. Main agent's fix: collapse minHeight to auto during capture + trailing-slice skip guard + spacing compression. Verified 1 page per template. Contrast bug (found + fixed by this iteration): `.a4-page td` and `.a4-page .font-mono` set explicit dark color on descendants of dark-bg tr/div containers. Because color is inherited but child's own declaration always wins over inheritance (regardless of parent !important), Grand Total numbers and invoice-number chip rendered black-on-black. Fix: scope-forced white color for known dark-bg parents (bg-slate-900, bg-blue-600, bg-[#0F172A], bg-amber-600/700) applied to td/th/.num/.font-mono/span/div children with !important.
